_doc: Cross-language seams between the Pi extension (pi-voice/src, TypeScript), headless Voice.app (macos/Voice, Swift) and the Python backend (src/chatbot). Read by a conformance test in each language; production code never loads it. Field types: string, boolean, or an enum name from `enums`; a trailing ? marks an optional field. A message lists every field its sender writes; a sender writing any other key is a contract violation.

stdio._doc: NDJSON over Voice's stdin (toVoice) and stdout (fromVoice), one object per line, `type` names the message.

voiceHistory._doc: The startup pack: a JSON array of turns in this environment variable, set by the extension when it spawns Voice.

tools._doc: Tools headless Voice publishes in session.update; the Python prompt gates its Pi section on spawn_thinking and names every one. Values are argument fields. check_thinking is read-only: it reports progress and findings without touching the job. spawn_thinking's optional `effort` picks how hard Pi thinks on that job (Codex's `backend_thinking_effort`); omitting it keeps the fast default, off.

channels._doc: Tags Swift puts at the start of context it injects for the voice model; the Python prompt explains them. legacyPi is still explained for old transcripts.

worker._doc: NDJSON between the extension and the pi-durable worker host (pi-voice/src/worker/host.mjs). This is the parallel path: one host process runs N jobs at once, each in its own conversation. `list` and `status` are the read-only coordination verbs; `spawn` on a live id steers it.
